label: Expression and regulation (genetic code, central dogma)
text: BI.O.A1.2 Expression and regulation. The genetic code maps codons to amino acids. It is a mapping, nearly universal, with known variant codes. It is owned here; CH.O.A3 cites it. Crick's central dogma (1970) states that sequence information, once in protein, cannot transfer back to nucleic acid or to other protein. Reverse transcription (RNA to DNA) is a "special transfer" allowed by it. The slogan DNA → RNA → protein is a heuristic (BI.M.H). Regulation covers transcription factors, chromatin state and noncoding RNA. Epigenetic marks can persist across mitotic divisions. Transgenerational epigenetic inheritance is a separate, narrower claim and is OPEN in many taxa.

warrant.warrant: W3, W4, W12 (code tables, gene nomenclature)
warrant.standard: Codon assignment confirmed by translation assay; names per HGNC or species committee
warrant.defeaters: Variant code unrecognised; epigenetic effect not separated from sequence
